title: KV cache quantization sensitivity map and operational SLA impact study
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: produce a fine-grained sensitivity map of KV-cache quantization (INT8 vs FP8) across model families and operational conditions, and quantify SLA/regression risk so we can ship conservative default profiles and automated fallback heuristics. Background: previous calibration-focused tickets produced calibration pipelines and profile sweeps but left open the question of how small quality regressions translate to customer-visible SLA violations under real traffic distributions. This ticket ties calibration artifacts to end-to-end latency and quality SLOs.
success_criteria: 1) Produce sensitivity map covering 3 model sizes (base, med, large) and 4 seq-length buckets with calibrated INT8 and FP8 profiles. 2) Identify operating regions where INT8 yields >15% latency improvement with <1% task-level accuracy regression on production prompt sets. 3) Deliver a decision matrix and safe-defaults for runtime-1.20 and a rollout plan (canary thresholds).
experiment_plan: Matrix: models=[rw-base, rw-medium, rw-large], seq_len_buckets=[<=64, 65-256, 257-1024, 1025-2048], profiles=[fp8-default, int8-symmetric, int8-asymmetric, hybrid-per-layer].

Calibration: collect KV activation statistics from 72-hour warm traces sampled across hosted customers and dedicated nodes; run per-head scale calibration and per-layer clipping sweeps; store quant metadata as profile artifacts (profile ids).
Workloads: evaluate on three curated prompt suites: 'synth-short' (chat-style short responses), 'doc-summarization' (long-context summarization), 'code-completion' (token-dense).

Metrics: p95 latency (ms), p50 latency, tokens/sec, cost/tokens (approx), task-level quality (BLEU/ROUGE/EM as appropriate), degradation rate (outputs that fail validation predicates), and fallback rate when runtime triggers model-variant fallback.
Measurement constraints: per-run >=50k requests to stabilise KV cache-hit variance; use synthetic load generator plus sampled production replay with anonymized payloads.
A/B plan: internal canary on dedicated pools with controlled traffic routing; safety threshold for rollout = no more than 0.5% increase in regression rate and <10% p95 regression vs current baseline.

results_summary: Calibration artifacts: generated 36 profiles (3 models x 4 seq-buckets x 3 quant modes) and stored as profile ids in artifact-store (kv-profile-ids: prof-20251130-*).

INT8-hybrid (per-layer hybrid precision) results: p95 latency improvement = +18% (rw-large seq<=256) to +25% (rw-medium seq<=64); task-level quality regression = 0.9% average on summarization, 0.4% on synth-short, 1.8% on code-completion (higher sensitivity).

INT8-symmetric (global scale) results: best latency wins but produced saturation events in long-context workloads; quality regression up to 3.2% on doc-summarization at seq>1024 — flagged as unsafe for long-context by default.
FP8-default results: p95 latency improvement = +12% to +15% across buckets; quality regression <= 0.4% across tasks — conservative and generally safe as default profile.

Fallback behavior: when fallback to FP8/FP16 triggered on saturation, we observed an end-to-end p95 increase of ~6% but eliminated the top 99th percentile quality failures. This supports automated fallback as a safety net for INT8 aggressive profiles.

Operational observation: KV cache hit-rate variance is the dominant contributor to latency tail for long-context workloads; quantization helps compute-bound tails but cannot fully offset cache-miss induced spikes.
decisions: Ship FP8-default as the conservative runtime-1.20 default for hosted API and Dedicated standard pools.
Mark INT8-hybrid as an opt-in profile for performance-sensitive customers with a recommended canary rollout and tighter monitoring thresholds.
Add automatic runtime fallback from INT8-hybrid -> FP8-default when per-request saturation or validation predicate failures exceed 0.2% over a 10m window.
Record per-profile safety metadata (max_seq_safe, sensitive_heads_list) so Console can show profile guidance and customers can opt-in per-route.
open_risks: Model drift: calibration performed on Nov traces; model or workload drift could invalidate scales — require monthly recalibration or trigger-based recalibration when quality monitors cross thresholds.
Cost regressions for FP8: while faster than baseline, FP8 still incurs some additional memory/encode overhead in certain kernels; we must monitor cost/tokens during canary.
Edge-case tokenizations: code-completion revealed sensitivity to long identifier tokens where per-token norm distribution shifts; need augmented calibration data for code workloads.
